topics.label: Lecture introduction
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic sets the stage for the lecture on the mechanisms driving the initiation and resolution of inflammation.

topics.label: Principles of innate immune recognition via PAMPs, DAMPs, and PRRs
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish how the innate immune system distinguishes self from non-self by detecting conserved microbial and damage-associated molecular patterns using germline-encoded receptors.

topics.label: Toll-like receptor organization and signaling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the classification, spatial distribution, and downstream signaling pathways of Toll-like receptors in response to pathogens.

topics.label: Cytoplasmic PRRs and the inflammasome pathway
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe intracellular pattern recognition receptor families and the multi-protein assembly of the inflammasome required for cytokine activation.

topics.label: Sentinel cell activation, leukocyte recruitment, and systemic inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover how tissue-resident sentinel cells trigger leukocyte trafficking and lymphatic drainage, as well as the physiological hazards of excessive systemic cytokine release.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic inflammatory states
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the active and passive mechanisms that terminate acute inflammation, mediate tissue reconstruction, and give rise to persistent chronic conditions or granulomas.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the concluding remarks and previews the next lecture on the complement system.
